A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SE-LLM research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and rendered figures, support reliable comparison. Internal numerical inconsistencies in v4 do not prevent identifying changes.

before.justification: v3 reports original forecasting results, component and backbone ablations, efficiency measurements, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains original forecasting experiments and adds TSCC component ablations, M4 backbone comparisons, anomaly analyses, and repeated-run results.

M1.justification: v4 deletes the post-cross-attention mean-and-add update of semantic embeddings described after v3 Eq. (3). It also corrects feedback and output assembly in the autoregressive pseudocode (v3 Algorithm 2; v4 Algorithm 7). These locally revise the specified procedure while retaining the TSCC, AM-VAE and Time-Adapter architecture.

E1.justification: The datasets and long-term, short-term and zero-shot forecasting coverage are retained. However, v3's separately reported M4 in-context forecasting evaluation and Figure 5 disappear from v4, although its dataset paragraph still mentions the task. The new ablations reuse existing dataset coverage.

E2.justification: The M4 short-term comparison drops DLinear, PatchTST and TimesNet (v3 Table 2; v4 Table 10), while retaining them in zero-shot comparisons. DECA becomes FSCA with the same cited work and scores. TQNet already appeared in v3 Table 1, so its newly supplied citation does not establish a new comparator.

E3.justification: v4 introduces component removal/replacement controls on ETTh1 and a five-backbone M4 evaluation (Tables 5 and 13). Existing dataset splits, forecasting horizons and metrics remain unchanged. AutoTimes customizations and Llama adapter exclusions are newly documented for retained experiments; the PDFs do not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v4 adds separate tests of AM-VAE, cross-attention, gated fusion and semantic embeddings, plus M4 backbone sensitivity. Its Figure 5 replaces v3's embedding-cluster visualization with STL residual, channel, temporal and anomaly-alignment analyses. Conversely, v3's long-term prediction case studies and Figure 9 are removed. This substantially changes the evidence examining component behavior.

E5.justification: v3 supplies point estimates and horizon averages without run counts or uncertainty estimates. v4 first specifies seeds 2024, 2025 and 2026, reporting individual runs, means and standard deviations across five datasets and four horizons in Table 16. This substantially expands statistical reporting without establishing an increase over v3's undisclosed run count.

E6.justification: Retained detailed forecasting and earlier ablation scores match across versions. v4 nevertheless adds substantial component, backbone and seed-level results and removes in-context results. New summaries also introduce numerical discrepancies: iTransformer's Traffic MSE is 0.384 in v4 Table 1, versus 0.394 in both v3 Table 1 and v4 Table 9. These discrepancies do not establish performance gains.

T1.justification: The AM-VAE sampling assumptions, correlation and gating mathematics, and evaluation metric definitions are retained. Equation consolidation and expanded procedural pseudocode introduce no substantive theoretical derivation, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, four introductory contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: TSCC enhances temporal-semantic representations, Time-Adapter models temporal dependencies, and SE-LLM achieves strong forecasting performance and efficiency. The additional evidence does not redefine those core claims.

C2.justification: v4 adds consequential limitations concerning Time-Adapter exclusions in Llama short-term and zero-shot experiments, computational costs, and Llama's unsuitability for long-term forecasting. It expands interpretations of anomaly alignment, generalization and statistical stability. Meanwhile, v3's qualification about negligible Time-LLM improvements on ETTm disappears from the corresponding discussion.

D1.justification: v4 adds extensive TSCC implementation pseudocode, top-k=32, adapter rank 8, AutoTimes inference and positional-encoding customizations, and disclosures about Llama adapter exclusions. These substantially improve implementation documentation. A new reproducibility statement claims code availability, but the PDF supplies no code-access link.

R1.justification: v4 adds the Lin et al. TQNet reference and removes references including CSformer, Fang et al. (2022), and Du et al. (2023). Most other bibliography changes update metadata or author information for retained works. The broader positioning relative to forecasting, semantic alignment and adapter research remains stable.

P1.justification: Experimental setup moves into an extensively reorganized appendix. Results, Time-Adapter and efficiency passages are rewritten, duplicated fusion exposition is removed, and dedicated implementation, reproducibility, discussion and limitations sections are introduced. This substantially changes the narrative structure despite retaining much introductory and methodological text.

P2.justification: Main Tables 1–4 become compact summaries with detailed counterparts in the appendix. Other tables are reoriented, ranking emphasis changes to red/blue, new analysis tables and an anomaly figure appear, and the efficiency plots are merged. The in-context and prediction-case figures are removed. These constitute substantial display and layout revisions.

improvement.justification: The component controls in Table 5 and repeated-run reporting in Table 16 address v3's limited evidence about component contributions and result variability. Implementation details and specific limitations also improve assessability. These benefits are tempered by removed in-context evidence and newly inconsistent summary values, including the conflicting Traffic results in Tables 1 and 9. The retained detailed tables preserve auditability, but the reporting errors limit the overall improvement.
